title: RBAC v2: Rule‑Indexer evaluator + adapter proxy for API/runtime/console
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Build a compact, high-throughput policy evaluation component (rule-indexer + fast-eval cache) and a small adapter proxy to enforce RBAC v2 across the REST/gRPC API surface, the inference runtime request path, and the Redwood Console. This ticket covers core evaluator implementation, adapter proxy interceptors for API/runtime/console, audit event enrichment, and SSO/SAML admin control hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator returns allow/deny with decision metadata in <2ms p95 for cached rules and <15ms p95 for cold evaluations on standard rule set (~300 roles, 1.2k policies)
Adapter proxy integrates as a gRPC interceptor and HTTP middleware; rejects unauthorized requests with consistent error schema and yields decision_id for traceability
All authorization decisions produce structured audit events (actor, resource, action, decision, policy_id, decision_id, reason) persisted to the audit pipeline
Console administrative flows (role management, role assignment, session impersonation) call the same evaluator and show deterministic results matching runtime enforcement
Automated test suite covering positive/negative paths, attribute-based rules, fallback policies, and SSO group-mapped role assignments
Security review completed and threat-model issues triaged before canary rollout
technical_design: Rule Indexer: compiles declarative RBAC v2 policies into an optimized rule table keyed by principal attributes and resource patterns
Fast-Eval Cache: LRU cache keyed by (principal_digest, resource_pattern, action) with TTLs and cache-invalidation hooks on role updates
Evaluation API: lightweight in-process evaluator providing Evaluate(principal, resource, action, context) -> {decision, policy_ids, reason, decision_id}
Adapter Proxy: small sidecar/edge process with HTTP middleware and gRPC interceptors that call the local evaluator synchronously. Fallback to remote evaluation service when adapter is in passive mode
Decision Tracing: attach decision_id to request context and response headers (X-Redwood-Decision-Id) for tracing and correlate with logs/metrics
Audit Enrichment: structured event builder emitting to internal audit topic with schema v2; support both sync write for high-sensitivity ops and async batching for normal ops
Console Plugin: JS layer that uses same evaluation endpoints to show admin preview of effective permissions; uses SSO group mappings when evaluating user access
Persistence: role and policy changes write to config store; indexer listens to changefeed and invalidates caches atomically
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature branch + unit tests + integration tests against test policy fixtures
Phase 2: deploy adapter as opt-in sidecar in staging clusters; enable detailed audit events for a subset of tenants
Phase 3: canary on 5% of production traffic with passive mode (log only) + telemetry monitoring
Phase 4: enable enforcement for low-risk routes and monitor errors/denials for 48h
Phase 5: full enforcement and Console admin UX enabled; run postmortem and tidy up deprecation flags
milestones: 2025-02-25: RFC merged and API contract finalized
2025-03-04: PR for core evaluator landed (internal review)
2025-03-10: Adapter middleware prototype deployed to staging
risks_mitigations: Risk: evaluator latency spikes under worst-case attribute cardinality. Mitigation: add adaptive fast-path heuristics and circuit-breaker to fallback to remote eval with rate limits
Risk: cache staleness causing incorrect allow decisions after role changes. Mitigation: atomic invalidation via changefeed and short TTLs for high-sensitivity policies
Risk: audit event volume increase. Mitigation: tier audit writes (sync for admin actions, batched async for regular decisions) and sampling controls per-tenant
Risk: SSO group sync delays leading to stale role assignments. Mitigation: show TTL-based confidence in Console and provide manual re-sync triggers for admins
